changes.title: Before the ministers
changes.briefing: You saw Her Majesty before the Conference sat and gave her Wallis's figures and Starhemberg's chests without ornament. She heard you out, called you into the Conference for the military business, and now wants your opinion on Silesia in writing by Thursday. The ministers you went ahead of have noticed.

scene.title: Before the Conference
scene.setting: Her Majesty's apartments in the Hofburg, a little after eight in the morning. The windows are hung with black; the Grand Duke stands by the stove.

lines.text: The Obersthofmeister's man hesitates at the door, then lets you through. The ministers have not yet come up.
Count Khevenhüller. They tell me the Conference will explain everything to me at ten. Tell me first what they will explain.

You give her Wallis's letter of the 16th: some seven thousand on the rolls in all Silesia, a little above three thousand foot and six hundred horse free to leave their walls, Glogau's works in want of repair, Brieg and Neisse no better. Then Starhemberg's figures: about a hundred thousand florins in the exchequer, debts many times that, the next provincial grants already pledged, the regiments paid late or not at all.
A hundred thousand. And my father kept an army of how many on paper? No — do not tell me the paper. Tell me what Wallis could put on the road tomorrow.
You tell her: three thousand foot, six hundred horse, if he stripped the garrisons bare.
And the King of Prussia has eighty thousand who are paid. We have heard nothing hostile from Berlin. But one does not need to hear it.

You are the first this morning who has given me a sum without a sermon around it. Come into the Conference when they reach the army; you will say it again there, the same way. Then put it in writing for me — what Silesia needs, what it costs, and where the money is to come from. Not what it would be pleasant to have.
Your cousin at Brünn writes to many people, I think. To you also?
You keep to Silesia and the chests. Of Brünn you say nothing. The Grand Duke inclines his head and does not ask again.
Go down, Count. They will wonder where I found the figures before they gave them to me.

commitments: You will be called into the Conference for the military business and repeat the figures there.
You are to give Her Majesty in writing what Silesia needs, what it costs and where the money is to come from.

reports.source: your wife, in her own hand
reports.title: We dined without you
reports.text: Your man says you were called into the Conference and kept there, so we did not wait. I am glad of it, truly, though Maria Antonia set your place and then would not let anyone take the chair away. The tailor came at five and the steward told him he must wait. He went off with a face like Lent. Do not let it become a habit with the tradesmen, my dear: in this town a bill unpaid in black is talked of more than a bill unpaid in colours. Come home when they let you go; I will keep the fire up.

reports.title: The resolutions of the twenty-first
reports.text: Your Excellency withdrew when the Conference passed from the army to the courts, and I send you, as is proper, what was resolved in the whole sitting. The notifications of Her Majesty's accession go to every court that guaranteed the Sanction, Versailles, London, Berlin and Dresden first among them, and leave this week; I drafted them last night. The Hofkriegsrat is to write to Count Wallis that he repair what he can, hold the garrisons and report. Count Starhemberg is to report what can be found for Silesia. No sum was fixed. I had hoped for your voice on the notifications, since the old gentlemen required persuading; I found other voices. Your figures were heard with more attention than mine usually are. I note it without complaint.

enclosure.title: Extract from the protocol of the Conference, 21 October 1740
rows: to all guarantor courts; despatch this week
Hofkriegsrat to order FML Wallis to repair the works, hold the garrisons, report
Count Starhemberg to report what can be found; no sum fixed
enclosure.note: Copy for the Vice-President of the Hofkriegsrat, in the secretary's hand.

guidance.known: The notifications go out without you; the Conference moved nothing and fixed no money for Silesia.
guidance.suspected: Bartenstein marks who helped him and who did not. 'I found other voices' means he has found other friends.
guidance.stakes: A Conference that orders Wallis to hold without money has given him nothing he did not have. Your written opinion is the next chance to change that.
guidance.explain: An order to repair works without funds goes to the commandant's own credit and to the town magistrates; it moves slowly, if at all.

reports.title: The household accounts
reports.text: As Your Excellency directed, I have paid what is small and owing at once: the chandler for the mourning candles, the carter, the wages of the stable. The tailor for the black hangings and the household's mourning was told he would be paid at Martinmas, when the rents come in; he said every house in Vienna has ordered black this week and his own cloth merchant will not wait for Martinmas. I would not have Your Excellency surprised if he complains about the town. The house can run as it is until the rents; it cannot also pay the tailor before them without borrowing, and I have not borrowed.

reports.source: Court Chancery, a Hofrat writing for Count Sinzendorf; summarising the Resident Demeradt's dispatch from Berlin
reports.title: From the Court Chancery: Berlin
reports.text: His Excellency the Court Chancellor has received the Vice-President's request for the reports of Her Majesty's ministers abroad, and is pleased to communicate the following in summary. The Resident at Berlin, writing before the news of His late Majesty's death could have reached that court, reports the King of Prussia at Rheinsberg and unwell with a fever; the regiments in their usual garrisons; nothing out of the ordinary in the movements of troops. The envoys at Dresden and Munich have received the notification and will report its reception in due course. His Excellency begs that any further requests touching the ministers abroad be addressed to the Court Chancery, which alone corresponds with them.

guidance.known: Demeradt saw nothing unusual in Berlin, but he wrote before the King knew the Emperor was dead.
guidance.suspected: The summary is all Sinzendorf will give; he does not want the Hofkriegsrat writing to his envoys.
guidance.stakes: You will get Berlin's news late and filtered unless you have a channel of your own.
guidance.explain: A dispatch from Berlin by the ordinary post takes a week or more to Vienna; whatever the King does after the news reaches him will not be known here before the first days of November.

reports.title: Riders, envoys and the antechambers
reports.text: Fact: an express rider left for Glogau at first light on the 22nd with Your Excellency's request to Count Wallis for current returns, the state of the works at Glogau, Brieg and Neisse, and anything seen or said across the Brandenburg border. With fair roads he should be there by the 25th and back by the end of the month. Fact: letters by the ordinary post went the same day to the commandants at Olmütz, Glatz and Prague asking for their returns and any report of troops on the roads. Fact: a private letter to the Resident at Berlin went by the post through Prague and Dresden; it will be ten days or more before any answer. Report: Count Perusa, the Bavarian envoy, called on the Court Chancellor on the 22nd and stayed an hour; he has not been seen in Her Majesty's antechamber. Rumour, from a Chancery clerk: Perusa waits for orders from Munich and will not condole until he has them. Fact: Count Sinzendorf and President Harrach both remarked in the antechamber on the 21st that Your Excellency went up before them.

reports.source: the War Pay Office (Hofkriegszahlamt), on the Vice-President's standing request
reports.title: What is owed to the regiments
reports.text: In answer to the Vice-President's request for the state of pay, the Pay Office submits what its books show. They show what was assigned, not what reached the regiments; the paymasters in the provinces are slower to account than to draw. The Silesian garrisons are owed several months. The regiments returned from Hungary are worse. The Office has no cash on hand beyond the week's needs of the capital, and its drafts on the provincial receipts for November are already given out.

enclosure.title: Arrears of pay, as the Pay Office's books stand, 24 October 1740
rows: Regiments in Hungary and the Banat
enclosure.note: Ranges, from the Office's books; the regiments' own returns may differ.

guidance.known: The army is owed months, Silesia among the better-served but still behind; the Pay Office has nothing to spare.
guidance.suspected: The books flatter: what was assigned in the provinces was not all paid.
guidance.stakes: Any proposal for Silesia that does not say where the money comes from will be read as Starhemberg reads promises.
guidance.explain: Unpaid garrisons desert, sell their bread and borrow from the town; a commandant owed for months cannot repair works on credit for long.

reports.via: by a page from Her Majesty's cabinet
reports.source: Her Majesty, in her own hand
reports.title: By Thursday
reports.asks: What will you advise Her Majesty for Silesia in the written opinion she wants by Thursday the 27th?
reports.text: Count Khevenhüller. I want your opinion on Silesia in writing by Thursday, so that I may read it before the Conference sits again. What the province needs, what it will cost, and where the money is to come from — and if the money cannot be found, say so, and say what can be done without it. I do not want three opinions folded into one so that everyone may agree with it. I want yours. M. T.

guidance.known: She asked for this herself, in her own hand; the paper goes to her, not to the Conference.
guidance.suspected: She is testing whether you will say the same in writing that you said to her face, and whether you will name the money.
guidance.stakes: A good paper makes you her man on Silesia; a vague one puts you back among the old ministers. Either way the ministers will read it.
guidance.explain: An opinion to the sovereign is expected to give a course, its cost and its means. Proposing men moved toward the frontier is a military act a foreign court can call provocation; the mandate forbids giving a pretext.

reports.source: Joseph Graf Harrach, President of the Hofkriegsrat
reports.title: On the forms of the Council
reports.asks: Will you send your opinion on Silesia through President Harrach, or carry it to Her Majesty yourself?
reports.text: My dear Count. I learn that Her Majesty has commanded from you an opinion on Silesia. I do not doubt it will be a good one. I would only recall to you that the opinions of the Hofkriegsrat have always gone to the sovereign through its President, so that the Council speaks with one voice and no one may say the President was passed over in his own house. I should be glad to see your paper before it goes up, and to add my name to it if I can. I have served three Emperors and do not mean to quarrel in the first week of the fourth reign. Harrach.

guidance.known: Harrach is your President and old in office; he wants the paper to pass through him.
guidance.suspected: He was stung by your going up first on the 21st; this is the form his displeasure takes.
guidance.disputed: Her Majesty asked for your opinion, not the Council's; Harrach says the two cannot be separated.
guidance.stakes: Through him: a slower paper, perhaps softened, but the Council behind you. Around him: the Queen's ear, and a President who remembers.
guidance.explain: By the custom of the Hofkriegsrat the Vice-President's opinions go up under the President; a direct paper is not forbidden when the sovereign asks, but it is noticed.

options.title: Ask for men and money now
options.objective: Put Silesia in a state of defence before winter: regiments from Moravia and Bohemia toward the Oder fortresses, money for the works and the garrisons' pay.
options.reasoning: Three thousand men cannot hold four fortresses against a King with eighty thousand. If he moves, he will move before the regiments can march in winter.
options.needs: A sum the Treasury does not have; marching orders through the Hofkriegsrat; quarters and bread in Silesia, where the Estates will complain.
options.risks: Berlin can call it provocation; the money is not there, so the regiments march unpaid and desert on the road.
options.ifWait: If the King of Prussia means nothing, nothing is lost. If he means something, the garrisons are what they are now.

guidance.known: The regiments nearest are themselves owed months.
guidance.suspected: Harrach proposes it knowing Starhemberg will refuse the money, so the blame for doing nothing falls on the Treasury.

options.title: Ask for money for the works and the pay only
options.objective: Repair Glogau, Brieg and Neisse and pay the Silesian garrisons up to date, raised by a loan against next year's grants; move no troops.
options.reasoning: Paid men in sound walls hold longer than unpaid men in a field. It gives no court a pretext. It is the most that can honestly be found.
options.needs: A banker's advance, which will cost dear and pledge grants not yet voted; the Silesian Estates' cooperation for labour.
options.risks: Too little if the King comes in force; the loan takes weeks to raise.
options.ifWait: The garrisons go into winter unpaid and the works unrepaired.

guidance.known: Starhemberg will support a sum he can see the source of.
guidance.suspected: No banker will lend quickly in a new reign without a guarantee from the Estates.

options.title: Ask for nothing that Berlin could read as a threat
options.objective: Wait for Wallis's returns and for the King of Prussia's answer to the notification before proposing anything.
options.reasoning: The King has every reason to remain a friend; a march toward his border is the surest way to make him an enemy.
options.needs: Patience, and an answer from Berlin.
options.risks: If the King has decided otherwise, every week lost is a week he gains.
options.ifWait: The opinion goes up late and says little; Her Majesty asked for it by Thursday.

guidance.known: Wallis's answer should be back by the end of the month.
guidance.suspected: Sinzendorf wants foreign affairs kept in the Chancery, and the army out of them.

debate.text: Silesia is held by its walls and the men inside them. We have neither in sufficient quantity.
Tell me the sum and I will tell you whether it exists. So far no one has told me the sum.
One does not put a sword in the window of a house where one is invited to dine.

undertakings.title: Fresh returns from Silesia
undertakings.stage: An express rider left for Glogau on the 22nd with your request to Wallis for current returns, the state of the works and anything seen across the border.
undertakings.waiting: Wallis's answer; out and back by express takes about a week.

undertakings.title: News from Berlin, Dresden and Munich
undertakings.stage: The Court Chancery sent a summary of the Resident's last dispatch from Berlin and asked that further requests come through it; your private letter to Demeradt went by the ordinary post.
undertakings.waiting: Demeradt's answer, ten days or more; the envoys' reports on how the notification was received.
undertakings.obstacle: Count Sinzendorf's Chancery keeps the envoys' letters to itself.

undertakings.title: The household accounts
undertakings.stage: The steward has paid the small bills and put the tailor off until Martinmas; he has not borrowed.
undertakings.obstacle: The tailor's own creditors, who will not wait.

audiences.title: Before the Conference
audiences.purpose: To give Her Majesty the state of Silesia and of the chests before the ministers did.

audiences.title: The opinion on Silesia
audiences.purpose: Her Majesty wants your written opinion on Silesia before the Conference sits again.

calendar.what: Your written opinion on Silesia due to Her Majesty
Wallis's answer from Glogau, if the rider has fair roads
Martinmas: the rents come in; the tailor to be paid

staffBriefing.changed: You saw Her Majesty alone before the Conference and were called into it for the army. The Conference sent the notifications to the courts, told Wallis to repair and hold, and fixed no money. Berlin, as of the Resident's last letter, was quiet; he wrote before the news reached the King. The Pay Office says the army is owed months and it has nothing to spare.
staffBriefing.stakes: Her Majesty has asked for your opinion herself. Count Sinzendorf and President Harrach both marked that you went up before them, and Harrach now wants your paper to pass through him. Bartenstein carried his notes without you and says so politely. The Grand Duke asked whether Neipperg writes to you, and had no answer.
staffBriefing.attention: Her Majesty wants the opinion on Silesia by Thursday the 27th: what is needed, what it costs, where the money comes from. Decide what you will ask for, and whether the paper goes to her through President Harrach or from your hand. Wallis's fresh returns will not be here before the end of the month.

hearsay.said: Khevenhüller went up to her before the ministers had their hats off. He means to be the Queen's man, and the Council may whistle.
They say in the Kohlmarkt that the Khevenhüller house cannot pay for its own black cloth.
hearsay.source: your steward, from the tailor's shop

dossier.note: Received you alone before the Conference, heard the figures, and asked for them again in Conference and in writing. On the 24th she fixed Thursday for the paper and asked for your opinion, not a joint one (fact).
Present at your audience. Said Berlin has sent nothing hostile but that one need not hear it; asked whether Neipperg writes to you, and did not press when you kept silent (fact).
Sent you the Conference's resolutions as its secretary. The notifications go to the courts this week; he says he had hoped for your voice and found others (fact).
Your President. Remarked in the antechamber that you went up first (report); wrote on the 24th asking that your opinion pass through him (fact).
His Chancery sent a summary of Demeradt's last Berlin dispatch and asked that all requests touching the envoys come through it (fact). Remarked that you went up before him (report).
His last dispatch, before Berlin knew of the Emperor's death, found the King at Rheinsberg with a fever and the regiments in their garrisons (report, through the Chancery's summary).
Called on Sinzendorf for an hour on the 22nd; not seen in Her Majesty's antechamber (report). Said to be waiting for orders from Munich before he condoles (rumour).
Paid the small bills, put the tailor off to Martinmas, and has not borrowed (fact).
Dined without you; warned that a mourning bill left unpaid is talked of (fact).
The War Pay Office sent the state of arrears: Silesia owed three to five months, Hungary worse, no cash to spare (fact, from its own books).

cast.name: The War Pay Office
cast.office: Hofkriegszahlamt: pays the army against assignments on the provinces
cast.agenda: Pay nothing it has not received; never be blamed for the arrears.
Keep every province; be obeyed as ruler, not managed as an heiress; trust few until they prove themselves — and find out who will tell her the truth.
A place of his own in the government beside his wife; his friends restored, Neipperg among them.
cast.voice: Easy, courteous, a little ironic; never quite says what he wants.

cast.agenda: The Hofkriegsrat's forms and his own primacy within it; no quarrel he can avoid.
cast.voice: An old courtier's mildness over a firm point.

whereabouts.doing: with the drafts of the notifications

overheard.line: He went in before us. In my day a Vice-President waited on the stairs.

items.head: Vienna, the 22nd of October
items.text: It has pleased Almighty God to call from this life, in the night between the 19th and 20th of this month, at the Imperial Favorita, His Roman Imperial and Catholic Majesty Charles the Sixth, to the inexpressible grief of the whole court and of all his faithful lands.

items.head: The government
items.text: Her Majesty Maria Theresa, Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, Archduchess of Austria, has taken up the government of the hereditary kingdoms and lands according to the Pragmatic Sanction, and the first Conference of the new reign was held on the 21st in Her Majesty's presence.

items.head: The mourning
items.text: The deepest court mourning is ordered. The preparations for the obsequies of the late Emperor are in hand, and the churches of the city hold prayers daily for the repose of his soul.

household.purse: The small bills are paid and the tailor will wait for Martinmas, though he grumbles about the town; the house runs on credit until the rents come in.

remarks: Her Majesty listened to plain figures and asked for more of them. That is a door, and the ministers saw it open.
President Harrach does not quarrel; he reminds. His note on the forms of the Council is a reminder.
Count Sinzendorf's Chancery will give us the envoys' news in summary and late. Anything quicker from Berlin must come by our own road.
Bartenstein carried his notifications without us. He will remember who helped, and he keeps careful accounts.
The Grand Duke asked after Count Neipperg and was given silence. He is not a man who asks twice.

ledger.text: You went to Her Majesty before the Conference with Wallis's returns and Starhemberg's chests → she heard you out and called you into the Conference for the army.
Conference → notifications to the guarantor courts this week; Wallis to repair and hold; no money fixed for Silesia.
Kept at the Hofburg → did not dine at home; the tailor put off to Martinmas.
Express rider to Glogau for fresh returns; letters to Olmütz, Glatz, Prague and to Demeradt at Berlin.
Her Majesty wants your opinion on Silesia in writing by the 27th; President Harrach asks that it pass through him.

hidden.chronicle: Charles VI died at the Favorita in the night of 19–20 October 1740; Maria Theresa took up the government under the Pragmatic Sanction. On the morning of 21 October Khevenhüller, Vice-President of the Hofkriegsrat, went to her before the first Conference and gave her Wallis's Silesian figures (about 7,000 on the rolls, some 3,600 fit to leave their walls) and Starhemberg's chests (about 100,000 florins, debts many times that, grants pledged). She was impressed by the plainness, called him into the Conference for the military business, and on the 24th asked for his own written opinion on Silesia by 27 October. Francis Stephen, present, asked whether Neipperg wrote to him; Khevenhüller said nothing for Neipperg. The Conference sent notifications to the guarantor courts (Bartenstein's drafts, carried without Khevenhüller's support), told Wallis through the Hofkriegsrat to repair and hold, and fixed no money. Sinzendorf and Joseph Harrach resent being passed over; Harrach asks that the opinion go through him. Sinzendorf's Chancery gives envoy news only in summary. Khevenhüller sent an express to Wallis (arrives Glogau 26 Oct, answer about 31 Oct), letters to Olmütz, Glatz, Prague and a private letter to Demeradt. The Pay Office reports months of arrears. At home the tailor is put off to Martinmas and talks in the town. Frederick at Rheinsberg, feverish, learns of the death about 26 October; nothing has moved in Prussia yet. Perusa waits for Munich's orders. Neipperg, receiving no word from his cousin, writes to the Grand Duke by his wife. Unresolved: what Khevenhüller proposes for Silesia, and by which route the paper goes up.

decisions.knows: Until about 26 October, nothing of the Emperor's death; he is at Rheinsberg with a fever.
decisions.wants: Silesia, while Vienna is weak and divided.
decisions.decides: Nothing yet; the news has not reached him. His army stays in its garrisons this turn.

decisions.knows: Wallis's and Starhemberg's figures, from Khevenhüller first and then the Conference.
decisions.wants: To find out which of her servants tell her the truth.
decisions.decides: Asks Khevenhüller for his own written opinion on Silesia by the 27th, separate from the Conference.

decisions.knows: Khevenhüller went to the Queen before the ministers and has asked for the envoys' reports.
decisions.wants: Foreign business kept in his Chancery; no move that could alarm Berlin.
decisions.decides: Gives a summary only and asks that all such requests come through him; speaks to Harrach about the breach of form.

decisions.knows: His Vice-President went up first and has been asked for an opinion directly.
decisions.wants: The Hofkriegsrat's forms and his own primacy.
decisions.decides: Writes asking that the opinion pass through him; has the Hofkriegsrat write to Wallis as the Conference resolved, without money.

decisions.knows: Khevenhüller did not support him; the Queen heard Khevenhüller's figures with attention.
decisions.wants: The notifications out, his primacy over the old ministers.
decisions.decides: Carries the notifications with Königsegg's and Alois Harrach's support; marks Khevenhüller as not yet a friend; sends him the protocol extract with a barb.

decisions.knows: No word has come from Khevenhüller.
decisions.wants: Release and the Silesian command, through the Grand Duke.
decisions.decides: Writes to the Grand Duke by his wife's hand, through the Grand Duke's household, without his cousin.

decisions.knows: The death and the notification; no instructions yet from Munich.
decisions.wants: To keep the Elector's claim open.
decisions.decides: Calls on Sinzendorf, does not condole, waits for Munich.

decisions.knows: His figures went to the Queen unaltered and were repeated in Conference.
decisions.wants: No war on promises; the Treasury first.
decisions.decides: Will report only what can be found; begins to look on Khevenhüller as a man who uses figures honestly.

fortune_used.for: Whether Her Majesty receives Khevenhüller before the Conference and hears him out
fortune_used.outcome: Received at once; she is struck by the plain figures and asks for them in Conference and in writing.

fortune_used.for: Whether Khevenhüller is admitted to the Conference
fortune_used.outcome: Admitted for the military business only; withdraws when the Conference passes to the courts. Not rejected, so he does not dine at home.

fortune_used.for: What the Conference resolves for Silesia
fortune_used.outcome: Wallis to repair and hold; Starhemberg to report what can be found; no money, no troops.

fortune_used.for: Whether the Court Chancery shares the envoys' reports
fortune_used.outcome: A summary only, with a request that all such requests go through the Chancery.

fortune_used.for: The express rider's speed to Glogau
fortune_used.outcome: Rain on the Moravian roads; arrives Glogau 26 October, a day late.

fortune_used.for: Whether the unpaid tailor's complaint spreads
fortune_used.outcome: It does: the Kohlmarkt says the Khevenhüller house cannot pay for its black.

Request for the latest reports of the ministers at Berlin, Dresden and Munich.

Returns of the garrisons and any report of troops on the roads, under the standing orders.

Under the standing orders: the state of the army's pay and arrears.

Starhemberg's report of what can be found; any loan proposal in Khevenhüller's opinion.
